clue.text: Milligan recorded his part in his downfall

definitions.text: Milligan recorded his part in his downfall

parts.words: Milligan recorded his part in his downfall
parts.note: Spike Milligan's war memoir is titled after the Nazi leader's first name: '... Hitler: My Part in His Downfall'

explanation.walkthrough: Spike Milligan, British comedian, wrote a comic war memoir whose title names the dictator by forename and claims a role in his defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of Hitler, the man in the title of Milligan's memoir.

clue.text: Excellent as Jepson's Child of the World

definitions.meaning: Child of the World' gives its boy hero this epithet

explanation.definitionFit: Excellent is a plain synonym; Jepson's book title pairs the epithet with its subtitle Child of the World.

clue.text: Philosopher from Communist bloc (Cambridge graduate)

indicators.note: the philosopher is drawn out of the letters of the words that follow, spanning a word break

explanation.surface: A thinker who came from behind the Iron Curtain and took a Cambridge degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals the letters spanning 'bloc (Cambridge'; 'Communist' and 'graduate' just dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Occam, the medieval thinker of the razor, is a famous philosopher.

clue.text: His love was lost in The Winter's Tale

definitions.text: His love was lost in The Winter's Tale

parts.words: His love was lost in The Winter's Tale
parts.note: the prince in Shakespeare's play loves Perdita, whose name means 'lost', so his love is literally the lost one

explanation.walkthrough: Perdita is Latin for 'lost one'; the clue reads like a lament but is a pun on her name.
explanation.definitionFit: The prince of Bohemia in Shakespeare's play who woos the shepherdess Perdita.

clue.text: Old tragedian confuses chess with polo

indicators.note: to confuse is to muddle, so the letters of the two game names are jumbled together

explanation.surface: An ancient playwright mixes up two quite different games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confuses' shuffles the letters of CHESS and POLO together.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the three great tragic dramatists of ancient Athens, author of Oedipus Rex.

clue.text: Joyce's penman, related to The Post

definitions.text: Joyce's penman, related to The Post

parts.words: Joyce's penman, related to The Post
parts.note: in Finnegans Wake the writer twin 'the Penman' is brother of Shaun the Post

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Post' looks like a newspaper but is Shaun the Post, the penman's twin in Joyce's Finnegans Wake.
explanation.definitionFit: The penman twin of Finnegans Wake, son of HCE and brother of Shaun.

clue.text: Past holds deceptively simple example of something overwritten

indicators.note: one word containing another, so the word past is split open around the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something deceptive is not what it seems, so the letters of simple are rearranged

explanation.surface: History conceals a seemingly simple instance of text written over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Past' looks like the definition's opening, but it is the container; the definition is the closing phrase about overwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript scraped and reused, with older writing beneath the new, is the classic overwritten document.

clue.text: Am I top, perhaps (vide 14), with the best possible results?

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged otherwise, so the three words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they lead the field, citing another clue, hoping for top results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles AMITOP; '(vide 14)' points to 14 across, another anagram, as a model for how to read this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum means the most favourable outcome; its plural names the best possible results.

clue.text: He knows his rites

parts.note: plays on 'knows his rights': an expert in forms of public worship knows rites

explanation.definitionFit: A scholar or compiler of forms of worship is an authority on church rites.

clue.text: V. S. Naipaul's Ralph, whose Isabella was independent

definitions.text: V. S. Naipaul's Ralph, whose Isabella was independent

parts.words: V. S. Naipaul's Ralph, whose Isabella was independent
parts.note: the narrator of The Mimic Men is a politician of the fictional Caribbean island Isabella after its independence

explanation.walkthrough: Isabella sounds like a wife but is the novel's invented island state.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Ralph, narrator of Naipaul's novel The Mimic Men.

clue.text: Humorist suggests many gypped in shopping precinct

indicators.note: one piece is placed within another, so the precinct word is opened up

parts.note: a mall is a shopping precinct
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to be gypped is to be cheated, or done

explanation.surface: A comic writer hints that crowds were swindled at the shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Many is a Roman-numeral convention here. A. G. Macdonell wrote the comic novel England, Their England.
explanation.definitionFit: A. G. Macdonell was a Scottish comic writer, best known for England, Their England.

clue.text: "From forth day's path and —'s fiery wheels" (Romeo and Juliet)

definitions.text: "From forth day's path and —'s fiery wheels" (Romeo and Juliet)

parts.words: "From forth day's path and —'s fiery wheels" (Romeo and Juliet)
parts.note: Friar Laurence's lines picture the sun god driving his chariot, the gap naming that giant of myth

explanation.definitionFit: Friar Laurence's speech names the sun god Hyperion, one of the Greek giants, driving his fiery chariot.

clue.text: Stay like Maxwell's rocks

definitions.meaning: to stay is to stop where you are
Gavin Maxwell's book is titled The Rocks ...

explanation.definitionFit: Stay is a synonym; Gavin Maxwell's otter book sequel says the rocks do the same.

clue.text: An unsettled spring month and a late winter one for Beth and Jo's sister

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the month's letters are rearranged

parts.note: May is a spring month
March is the month at the end of winter

explanation.surface: Two months, one in spring and one at winter's end, are offered for a sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges MAY to AMY. Louisa May Alcott's Little Women has sisters Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest sister in Little Women, alongside Meg, Jo and Beth.

clue.text: One of Kipling's Plain Tales from the Hills as feature of church

definitions.text: One of Kipling's Plain Tales from the Hills
definitions.meaning: a story title in Kipling's early collection of Anglo-Indian tales
the upper wall of a nave, pierced with windows above the aisle roofs

explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of clerestory, the windowed upper storey of a church nave.

clue.text: I suggest an element of sycophantic biography (well I'm boss anyhow)

indicators.note: anyhow means in any haphazard way, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker puts forward a fawning trait of life-writing while asserting authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges WELLIMBOSS. James Boswell's adoring Life of Samuel Johnson made his name a byword for devoted biography.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait of James Boswell, whose devoted Life of Johnson made his name stand for admiring biography.

clue.text: Sign language?

parts.note: not gesturing for the deaf but expression through emblems and signs, as in art or poetry

explanation.definitionFit: The use of emblems to stand for ideas is, playfully, a language of signs.

clue.text: Self-defining production scripted by Beckett

parts.note: Samuel Beckett's 1965 short picture with Buster Keaton bears the plain name of its own medium

explanation.surface: Beckett wrote a work whose title names what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckett's only cinema work, starring Buster Keaton, is titled simply by its medium.

clue.text: Composer gives refreshment to Swiss poet

parts.note: Conrad Ferdinand Meyer was a nineteenth-century Swiss poet
beer is a refreshing drink

explanation.surface: A musician hands a drink to a poet from Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Meyerbeer was a German composer of grand opera such as Les Huguenots.

clue.text: Even his opponents applauded his swimming

definitions.text: Even his opponents applauded his swimming

parts.words: Even his opponents applauded his swimming
parts.note: in Macaulay's Lays the Roman hero swims the Tiber and 'even the ranks of Tuscany could scarce forbear to cheer'

explanation.definitionFit: The Roman who held the bridge, then swam the Tiber, in Macaulay's Lays of Ancient Rome.

clue.text: They shaded O'Neill's longing

parts.note: Eugene O'Neill's play Desire Under the ... : the trees stood over the desire

explanation.surface: Trees cast shadow over the yearning in an American play.
explanation.definitionFit: The trees in the title of Eugene O'Neill's play Desire Under the Elms.

clue.text: Slang young ladies fit for novelist

parts.note: gals is a slang word for girls
fit means suitable or deserving, worthy

explanation.surface: Informal talk calls young women suitable for a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Galsworthy wrote The Forsyte Saga.

clue.text: Transformed nymph, namely a climbing partner

parts.note: sc. abbreviates Latin scilicet, meaning namely

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the word upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A nymph changed in shape, that is to say a partner in a climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads its piece upwards, as suits a down clue. Circe turned the nymph into a monster facing Charybdis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the nymph was turned by Circe into a many-headed sea monster.

clue.text: Formerly Tolkien demon, first a cleansing priest in fiction

parts.note: ex- means former
orcs are Tolkien's goblin creatures
first is written 1st, read as IST

explanation.surface: Once a Tolkien fiend, now a priest who purges in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' becomes IST by reading the numeral 1 in 1st as letter I. The Exorcist is William Peter Blatty's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Blatty's novel and its film are named for the priest who drives out a demon.

clue.text: Measure play part for decree

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
an act is a part of a play

explanation.surface: A measure plays a role in making a ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to make law, to ordain by decree.

clue.text: Bulldog Drummond's engineer

definitions.meaning: H. C. McNeile wrote the Bulldog Drummond thrillers under this pen-name
a military engineer who digs trenches and tunnels

explanation.definitionFit: McNeile's pen-name, from his army service as a Royal Engineer, a military digger.

clue.text: Resentment of Mrs Ellis

definitions.meaning: the title of a novel attributed to the Victorian writer Mrs Sarah Stickney Ellis

explanation.definitionFit: Resentment from wounded pride; also a novel by the Victorian moralist Mrs Ellis.

clue.text: Transport mentioned for mystery writer

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the word for transport is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A vehicle comes up in talk about a crime novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' signals that CAR is heard. John Dickson Carr wrote locked-room mysteries.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dickson Carr was a master of locked-room detective stories.

clue.text: Former tree dweller see in bain-marie, lightly simmering

indicators.note: the spirit sits inside the run of letters across the following words

explanation.surface: Look at what is gently cooking in a water-bath pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters spanning 'bain-marie, lightly'. In The Tempest Sycorax imprisoned the spirit in a pine until Prospero freed him.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's airy spirit in The Tempest was once trapped in a cloven pine.

clue.text: Working girl to lose a quid, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible variant, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl in a job might end up a pound down.
explanation.definitionFit: A female slave or concubine in an Ottoman harem, a girl kept in service.

clue.text: Friend of Finn from St Petersburg

definitions.text: Friend of Finn from St Petersburg

parts.words: Friend of Finn from St Petersburg
parts.note: Twain's boy hero, Huckleberry Finn's friend, lives in St Petersburg, Missouri, not Russia

explanation.surface: A companion of a Finn hails from the Russian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finn' and 'St Petersburg' suggest Finland and Russia; it is Huck Finn and Twain's Mississippi town.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's boy hero, pal of Huckleberry Finn in the river town of St Petersburg.

clue.text: Direct artist

definitions.meaning: to direct is to guide or ... a course
Philip Wilson ... was an English painter

explanation.definitionFit: To guide something is a synonym; Philip Wilson Steer was an English Impressionist painter.
